safety_verdicts.content: Chest pain radiates to the shoulder and neck.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes radiation to left arm/shoulder but does not include neck radiation as stated in the gold fact.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting neck radiation can under-document classic anginal features and may reduce perceived likelihood/severity of acute coronary syndrome in downstream review. In this case, emergent escalation (ambulance) was already initiated, so impact is mainly on documentation and handover completeness.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state haemodynamic stability.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document haemodynamic stability removes an important risk-stratifying datapoint in suspected MI and could prompt unnecessary escalation or, conversely, leave stability unclear for receiving clinicians. However, the patient was already being urgently transferred, so the likely effect is limited to additional monitoring/reassessment.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient was examined while seated at rest.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state patient was examined seated at rest.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not stating the patient was assessed seated at rest reduces clarity about the conditions under which symptoms/appearance were observed, which can affect interpretation of dyspnea/distress. The clinical impact is likely limited to reduced documentation quality and potentially extra reassessment on arrival.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient appears well perfused on video inspection.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state well-perfused on video inspection.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient appeared well perfused removes reassuring evidence against shock in an acute chest pain presentation. This most likely leads to conservative management or repeat assessment rather than direct harm, given emergency transfer was already underway.

safety_verdicts.content: Urgent ECG and troponin T are required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes ECG via EMS but does not mention troponin T requirement.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting the need for troponin testing can contribute to incomplete ACS workup planning and, if relied upon, could delay confirmation/rule-out of myocardial infarction. Although EMS/hospital protocols typically include troponins, this omission has potential to cause delay in diagnosis or treatment steps.
